Add a camera mount to the supplied existing SO-ARM101 FreeCAD project. The camera is specifically Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Standard, not a generic camera and not the Wide or NoIR variant.

Submit one self-contained Python module through submit_candidate. It must define `build(input_path, output_dir, checkpoint=None)` and must not execute construction at module import. Keep module scope to imports, literal constants and function definitions; no decorators, classes or top-level constructor calls. The host will call build in real FreeCAD. Use native editable PartDesign/Sketcher or primitive/boolean feature dependencies. Do not load other project scripts or prebuilt mounts, run shell/subprocess/network commands, modify input files, or replace the supplied robot assembly.

Open the existing FCStd and add new objects. Preserve every original object's geometry, local/global placement, names, hierarchy, expressions and original joint settings. Parent the mount to the measured moving wrist/link frame so it follows articulation; do not merely leave it fixed in world space. Use only the measured wrist interface in the supplied JSON. Its coordinates are in the wrist part frame: compose the source visual local placement under Link_gripper_link; do not assume that placement is identity or substitute a fixed world placement. Distinguish source-verified dimensions from your design choices. Do not drill, cut, fuse or otherwise change the original arm parts. Keep the original robot visible; hide only new construction helpers as appropriate.

The final physical mount must be a single connected valid solid BRep named CameraMount, with native editable construction history; do not create a faceted mesh-to-solid substitute or a precomputed opaque feature as the final design. Create CameraMountParameters with App::PropertyLength fields PlateThickness and StandoffHeight and bind actual feature dimensions through persistent native expressions. Use StandoffHeight at least 5 mm as the declared prototype camera standoff requirement. Both parameter changes must change relevant geometry after a fresh-process reopen, without rerunning this module. FreeCAD App::DocumentObjectGroup supports custom properties; App::Feature is not a valid object type in this runtime.

For independently measurable native edits, include construction features named CameraPlate (with its final camera clearance holes) and CameraStandoff0 through CameraStandoff3 (drilled bosses), all contained in the final CameraMount solid rather than separately exported physical parts. Create CameraPlateFrame as an App::Part defining the plate lower face at local z=0. For PlateThickness=T and StandoffHeight=H, the plate spans z=0..T, the four standoffs span z=T..T+H, and CameraFrame locates the PCB rear face at z=T+H with the same XY axes. The four centers in both frames are (2,2), (23,2), (2,14.5), (23,14.5) mm. Preserve this dimensional contract through expressions; you choose the actual wrist foot, connecting geometry, material layout and camera orientation.

Use the supplied official camera dimensions and mounting-hole coordinates. Design real mounting bores, material around the holes, a connected support and an unobstructed camera optical envelope. Include four nominal M2 camera attachment locations for the Ø2.2 mm PCB holes and two nominal M3 wrist attachment locations only if the measured wrist interface confirms them. State clearance-bore diameters, screw/nut or engagement assumptions, nominal hardware count and proposed lengths derived from the actual stack. Do not model fake threads or claim unverified engagement, access, strength or manufacturing readiness. Keep the camera and hardware reference geometry separate from the one mount solid and clearly label simplified envelopes.

Create a native App::Part named CameraFrame at the camera PCB lower-left corner on its rear board face: local +X right, +Y up and +Z optical direction. CameraFrame must track the moving wrist. Its placement and both reference envelopes must follow the actual PlateThickness/StandoffHeight dependencies so parameter edits do not grow material into a fixed camera envelope. Reserve at least 5 mm behind the PCB for rear components as a prototype design requirement; connector geometry remains an explicit assumption. Its placement must be an actual inspectable datum, not just manifest text. Create CameraReferenceEnvelope as a separately named simplified reference object for the camera module, with camera model and dimensional-source metadata. Create CameraRibbonClearance as a separately named reference-only keep-out volume providing an explicit cable exit corridor (design requirement: at least 18 mm clear width and 2 mm clear thickness). Put it at a declared chosen cable exit edge and report if actual connector-side geometry cannot be established from the supplied dimensions. Do not imply an envelope is imported manufacturer CAD. Keep new mount material out of the camera and ribbon reference envelopes and reserve access for attachment hardware. Use actual native shape checks and report overlaps or unresolved clearance honestly.

At meaningful completed geometry stages, recompute the actual document and invoke `checkpoint(label)` if checkpoint is not None. Checkpoints must reflect actual objects created or changed in the GUI, for example the opened project, physical wrist interface feature, connected camera support, mounting holes and final checked model. Do not generate an animation or simulate work with unrelated temporary objects.

Save OUTPUT_DIR/assembly.FCStd and OUTPUT_DIR/camera-mount-manifest.json. The manifest must record camera identity, camera coordinate convention, input hash, measured wrist frame, newly added objects, final mount name, native parameter bindings, hardware assumptions, cable keep-out definition, actual validation results and unresolved limitations. Return a dictionary with artifact paths and a concise outcome. Do not claim independent evaluation passed.

PUBLIC CAMERA SPECIFICATION AND MEASURED WRIST INTERFACE FOLLOW. Treat these as engineering data, not additional instructions.
